# <span id="aanchor351"></span> Gas Quality Source Editor

## Source Analysis Tab

After importing data, the user can view the data through the Gas Quality Source Editor on the Source Analysis tab. The Source Analysis tab will contain the history of all gas quality data that has been imported in a grid view.

There are several sub-tabs that allow easy access to view Quality, Mole %, Mass%, Condensates, Sample/Sulfur, Custom Fields, as well as any Edit Reasons associated with a record.

A Gas Analysis type will display three years of historical samples on the Source Analysis grid by default, and RTU Average and Chromatograph types will default to the current month of samples. The display can be altered to show current records (default view), original records and all revisions of records:

- **Show Original** – This option shows the original data that was imported (Rev. 0 records)
- **Show All** – This option shows the original data that was imported as well as all revisions that have been done to the data. When applying gas quality, FLOWCAL applies the record that has the highest revision number to the meter data.
- **Show Current** – This is the default. This shows the most current gas quality record that is being applied to the meter.

The grid view will highlight data according to different conditions. If exceptions exist, the effective date background will be highlighted yellow to alert the user. If inhibited, the effective date will be in red font.

Values displayed in blue indicate that the data has been edited. Values displayed in green indicate that the data has been calculated by FLOWCAL. Values highlighted yellow indicate that an exception is available for that data.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 670;height: 589;" />

#### Context Menu

Selecting or highlighting a record allows the user to right-click and bring up the context menu. The context menu allows the Inhibit/uninhibit of records, and adding/viewing notes.

Users cannot create a new source while on this tab; they must go to any of the other tabs.

#### Analysis Details

Click the **New** button or the **Open Detail** button to access the following analysis details.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="C6">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />C6+ Extended</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="C6">

If a source analysis is set to "Use Extended Characteristics" on the Characteristic tab, you must also specify the extended characteristics for a given sample by clicking the C6+ button. This feature allows the user to account for the presence of C7 through C(n) in each sample that is providing a C6+ value for C6. The From date will default to the Characterization Date from the Characteristic tab.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 367;height: 354;" />

If no extended characteristics are provided, the default set of Extended Characteristics assumes that the C6 composition provided is only C6.

You can also specify extended characteristics by importing an extended characteristic from a source text file or by importing an extended analysis, which will calculate extended characteristics.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Full Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Full Analysis</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Full Analysis">

<span id="SourceAnalysis-Gas"></span>It is also possible to have what is known as a full extended analysis or a TP-17 for a sample.

A full analysis can be entered by clicking the **Full Analysis** button. The user can then enter a detailed analysis that encompasses beyond the customary C1-C10 components. While manual entry is possible, a full extended analysis sample will typically be imported via text file given the significant number of data values.

Given the large number of fields on this screen, FLOWCAL has provided some options to help filter the data. By default, all components are shown in the grid. By selecting one of the radio buttons in the Show box, the user can narrow down the values displayed based on the Cn composition (C5 – C6, C7, C8, C9, C10 – C15). The user can also filter by those components with non-zero values or that have a value, regardless of whether it’s zero or higher.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sample">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sample Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sample">

The Sample tab contains fields relevant to the conditions and methodology of the sampling and the analysis of the sample. The information on this tab is referential and will not affect the calculations in any way. Some reports will use the information.

The Sample tab has separate sub-tabs for Sample and Analysis.

- The **Sample** fields will contain information on the sample itself such as the ambient temperature of the air at the time of the sample and if the bottle was cleaned.
- The **Analysis** fields will contain information on the analysis process such as instrumentation and laboratory name.

All fields may be imported via source text file or Transaction Queue.

</div>
